title: App Development Karachi: iOS, Android, Web Apps | 22 Signals
description: App development Karachi fintechs, logistics firms and distributors rely on: Android-first apps that work offline, take payments and pass app store checks.
h1: App development Karachi field teams, riders and customers can rely on
intro: We design and build iOS, Android and web apps for Karachi companies: fintech and wallet apps, sales-force and distributor ordering apps, rider and driver apps for logistics, and customer apps for insurers, clinics and retailers. Apps are built Android-first, keep working on weak connections, take payments securely and launch on the app stores with a support plan behind them.

sections.h: Apps that fail in the field
p: An app that works perfectly in an office on fibre can fall apart on a delivery route through Saddar or a sales visit in Orangi. The signal drops, the phone is three years old, storage is full, and the order the sales officer just took disappears. Within a month the Karachi sales team is back to taking orders on paper and WhatsApp.

Karachi needs apps built for real conditions: offline mode that syncs when the signal returns, small download sizes, fast start-up on mid-range Android phones and clear Urdu or English labels for people who did not choose the app themselves.

sections.h: Common app types for Karachi businesses
p: Karachi is a city of distributors, couriers, traders and branch networks, so many of the apps worth building are working tools rather than consumer products. A sales officer covering a route, a rider finishing deliveries across the city before evening traffic, or a surveyor inspecting cargo at the port needs an app that is quick, forgiving and clear. Consumer apps matter too, especially in finance and retail, where customers compare you with the best apps on their phone.
list: Fintech and wallet apps: onboarding, KYC capture, transfers, bill payments and statements.
Distributor and sales-force apps: route plans, outlet visits, order capture, scheme display and stock checks, all usable offline.
Rider and driver apps for courier, freight and last-mile companies: job lists, proof of delivery photos, cash-on-delivery collection and live location.
Insurance and takaful apps: policy details, claim submission with photos and claim status updates.
Customer apps for retailers and restaurants: ordering, loyalty and push offers.
Patient apps for clinics in Clifton, DHA and across the city: bookings, reports and reminders.

sections.h: Fintech apps and State Bank rules
p: Karachi is the base for much of Pakistan's banking and fintech activity, and payment apps carry regulatory weight. Depending on the model, the State Bank of Pakistan's rules for electronic money institutions, payment systems, digital onboarding and cloud outsourcing may apply, and SECP rules cover lending and investment platforms. We are the build team, not the licence holder, so we work alongside your compliance lead and your licensed banking partner.

In practice that means designing for strong customer authentication, device binding, transaction limits, audit trails and secure storage of credentials from the first sprint. Retrofitting those controls just before launch is slower and riskier. All apps follow the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 and the principles in the draft Personal Data Protection Bill for consent and data use.

sections.h: How we build: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: who will use the app, where and on what phones, and what success looks like in numbers you already track.
Plan: user flows, clickable prototypes and a technical plan. We test the prototype with a handful of real users, such as riders or sales officers, before writing production code.
Build: two-week sprints with a working build at the end of each one, installed on your test phones.
Grow: launch, crash and usage monitoring, then a roadmap of improvements based on what users actually do.

sections.h: Proof: product work beyond client apps
p: Alongside client work, we are developing an AI commentary product for live esports, which has to process a fast-moving game and respond in near real time. Building our own product keeps our engineers honest about performance, testing and release discipline, and that carries into every app we build for clients.

Your app is built under one Signal Lead, with sprint reviews booked at times that suit your team and a written note after each one. Test builds go to your phones through TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, so your team can try every version in real Karachi conditions. If user testing on site is needed, we plan it for that stage.

faqs.q: Should we build for Android or iOS first?
faqs.a: For most Karachi audiences, Android first. It is the dominant platform among customers, riders and field staff in Pakistan. If your users are corporate clients or an overseas market, iOS may matter more. Cross-platform frameworks often let us ship both from one codebase, and we recommend the approach once we know your users.

faqs.q: Can the app work without internet?
faqs.a: Yes. For sales-force, rider and inspection apps we build offline mode as standard: data is saved on the phone and synced when the connection returns, with conflict handling so nothing is lost or duplicated. We test it by switching phones to airplane mode in the middle of real tasks.

faqs.q: Can you build a wallet or payments app?
faqs.a: We can build the app and its integrations, but the licence must sit with you or a licensed partner bank or electronic money institution regulated by the State Bank of Pakistan. We work with your compliance team on authentication, limits, audit trails and data handling so the app supports the approvals you need.

faqs.q: How long does app development Karachi firms ask for usually take?
faqs.a: For an MVP with a focused feature set, it depends on integrations and approvals. Larger apps with payments, offline sync and admin panels take longer. We agree the scope and dates in writing at the planning stage, and you see a working build every two weeks.

faqs.q: Do you help with app store approval?
faqs.a: Yes. We prepare the store listings, screenshots, privacy disclosures and test accounts that Apple and Google reviewers need, and we handle any rejection feedback. Financial and health apps often get extra scrutiny, so we plan for that time in the schedule.

We agree at the outset, in writing, who owns the source code, designs and app store accounts, and you always have access to what we build and run for you. We hand over documentation and can continue supporting the app, or your in-house team can take it over.
